verses: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلْخَاطِئَةِ
فَعَصَوْا۟ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَٰكُمْ فِى ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ
فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ
وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَٰحِدَةً
وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرْجَآئِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَٰنِيَةٌ
يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَيَّامِ ٱلْخَالِيَةِ
وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَٱسْلُكُوهُ
إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ
وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ

leads.title: The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man ↔ The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted (weight 4.6). Pair score 4.5.

Only in The four beasts, the Ancient of Days and one like a son of man: Thrones are set and the Ancient of Days sits, his garment white as snow and his hair like pure wool; The seer asks one of the attendants or an angel, who explains the vision to him; A bear raised on one side with three ribs in its mouth is told 'Arise, devour much flesh'; The arch-enemy beast is slain and its body given over to burning fire; A heavenly figure or the holy ones are given everlasting dominion, glory and kingdom which all peoples serve; God's throne is flames of fire with wheels of burning fire; Four great beasts rise from the sea, each different, symbolizing successive kingdoms; A leopard with four wings and four heads is given dominion; The four winds of heaven stir up the great sea, out of which monstrous beasts arise; The holy ones of the Most High (qaddishe 'elyonin) receive and possess the kingdom forever; The horn makes war against the holy ones and prevails until the Ancient of Days comes; A little horn with human eyes and a mouth speaking great things uproots three horns; and 15 more.

Only in The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger: Whoever is given his book in his left hand wishes he had never been given it and that death had been final; his wealth and power are gone; Whoever is given his book in his right hand says 'Here, read my book!' and lives a pleasing life in a lofty garden with fruit clusters near; He did not believe in God the Great and did not urge the feeding of the poor; The damned have no friend and no food except ghislin (foul washings/pus); Had he fabricated sayings against God, God would have seized him by the right hand and cut his aorta (watin); 'I swear by what you see and what you do not see'; 'Seize him, fetter him, roast him in hellfire, then thread him on a chain seventy cubits long'; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Reclining on couches lined with brocade, with the fruit of the gardens hanging near; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted [divergence between the texts]; Kings bound with chains and nobles with fetters of iron to execute 'the judgment written'; and 5 more.

leads.title: Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory ↔ Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Ezekiel's inaugural vision by the Chebar canal: four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, the throne and the glory: The heavenly creatures move straight ahead in every direction without turning; The heavenly creatures have straight legs with calves' hooves and human hands under their wings; A firmament gleaming like awesome ice/crystal is spread above the creatures' heads; A vision dated 'in the thirtieth year' without stated era; Fire like torches moves among the creatures and lightning flashes from it; Each heavenly creature has four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle; The center of the fire gleams like hashmal (amber/electrum); The heavens are opened and the prophet sees visions of God; The visionary hedges every description: 'the appearance of the likeness of...'; On the throne is 'a likeness as the appearance of a man'; The prophet is himself a priest or of priestly family; The radiance around the enthroned figure is like the rainbow in the cloud; and 13 more.

Only in Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears; That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them; At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing; Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast); Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?'; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; The overturned city (al-mu'tafika, Sodom) God hurled down and covered with what covered it; A roaring cold wind (sarsar) on a day of continuous ill omen plucks men away like trunks of uprooted palms; The sky splits and is frail that day, and the angels are on its borders; When the Event (al-waqi'a) befalls, none can deny it: it abases and exalts; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed; and 3 more.
